pool.text: Novgorodian pirates plundered and burned Žuketau and Kazan during their military campaign.
Tsar Ivan the Terrible conquered the city after a long military siege.
The local Tsardom was abolished and Kazan became a regional governorate seat.
The major Russian poet Gavrila Derzhavin was born within the city.
The official coat of arms featuring a crowned black snake was approved.
The holy Islamic text Qur'an was printed for the first time in Kazan.
Kazan Federal University was founded as one of the oldest in Russia.
A horse tramway first appeared in the public transportation network.
The official city telephone network was officially opened for public communication.
The national country introduced a sudden ban on the historical heraldry.
Trolleybus operation officially opened to serve public commuters across streets.
The growing urban population officially reached the milestone of one million people.
The city ranked 186th in Mercer's Worldwide Quality of Living Survey.
The historic settlement celebrated its official millennium after historical commission settlement.
The Russian Patent Office granted the right to refer to itself as the Third Capital.
The city successfully hosted the international Summer Universiade sporting event.
The popular public bus transport carried about seventy-four percent of passengers.
Kazan served as one of the proud host cities for the FIFA World Cup.
A tragic school mass shooting and bombing carried out by a teenager occurred.
The city hosted the international BRICS Games with athletes competing in many sports.
